sampling_model.design: Abstract triangular rectangular fixed-design panel with \(N/T\to c\in(0,\infty)\) and one deterministic treated-post block.
sampling_model.units: The arrays \(d,qvec,a,b,\Lambda,F\) are fixed members of the exact-oracle class defined by the four stated orthogonality restrictions; those restrictions remove baseline-factor cross terms but do not select a profile minimizer. Randomness comes only from iid Gaussian \(E_{it}\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(D=dqvec^{\top}\), with heterogeneous treated-post component \(\theta(d\odot a)(qvec\odot b)^{\top}/\sqrt m\).
sampling_model.overlap: The scalar shares \(p_N\) and \(q_T\) have interior limits \(p\) and \(q\). The restricted Grams use the diagonal control selector \(M_d\) and diagonal pre-period selector \(M_{qvec}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Full-sample IFE profiles rank \(r+1\) with smallest-coefficient, lexicographic best-approximation, and lexicographic subspace-completion rules. The internal masked benchmark fits rank \(r\) only on \(D_{it}=0\), with radii containing the normalized true baseline. Both intervals use their stated residual degrees of freedom and nonnegative-root conventions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The profiled IFE coefficient is consistent and asymptotically normal under strong-factor and identification conditions.
The slope limit distribution is invariant to fitting more factors than the true rank under the paper's regularity conditions.
A fixed rectangular finite-rank perturbation separates from the noise edge exactly above the \(D\)-transform threshold.
Bias-aware intervals attain uniform coverage over factor strength under generalized regressor non-collinearity.
With an asymptotically strong treatment-effect factor, full-sample IFE converges to the common component \(\gamma\) rather than ATT.
Tall-wide factor imputation yields pointwise asymptotic normality for an ATT estimator under strong observed-block factor conditions.
IFE with a growing fitted factor count converges to a conditional-variance-weighted average of heterogeneous treatment effects.
Potential-factor models identify systematic causal effects and provide feasible counterfactual inference using untreated or treatment-specific factor structure.

body.tldr: This paper studies an abstract exact-oracle panel experiment in which four finite-array orthogonality restrictions remove ordinary baseline confounding without fixing the profiled coefficient.  The full-sample IFE coefficient has a uniformly localized two-by-two spiked-SVD profile with an always-separated singleton minimizer.  It equals the ATT coordinate exactly when \(|h|\le h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\), and beyond that threshold it moves strictly toward the common effect.  The absorbed phase is relatively open and is nonempty exactly when \(\overline h>\min_{\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}}h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\); on its compact subsets the conventional residualized IFE Wald interval has asymptotically zero coverage.  Masked fitting remains an internal benchmark control.

project_justification.gap: Existing panel theory covers regular strong factors, generic weak-factor robustness, or a strong bad-control endpoint, while rectangular random-matrix theory fixes the spike before taking limits.  It does not supply the globally selected coefficient-indexed phase boundary \(h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\) after baseline-confounding terms are removed by defining restrictions.
project_justification.niche: An exact-oracle noise-scale treatment factor creates a nonregular but fully classifiable transition: ATT is retained through the spectral edge and is partially absorbed strictly beyond it.
project_justification.fill: The project derives \(\Phi_{\eta,h}\), proves uniform bounded-local profile convergence and an always-separated singleton minimizer, identifies \(h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)=c^{1/4}/[\kappa s_1(C_\eta)]\), proves that the absorbed phase is nonempty exactly under the stated reach inequality, and derives the explicit residual-design overlap and conventional-Wald zero-coverage law there.

body.related_work: Bai (2009) supplies the regular profiled-IFE and strong-factor framework, but not a coefficient-indexed noise-scale treatment spike.  Moon and Weidner (2015) study harmless rank overestimation under conditions excluding this low-rank regressor geometry.  Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi (2012) supply the fixed-spike rectangular outlier and singular-vector-overlap maps; this paper embeds those maps in the global coefficient profile and proves that the ATT coordinate is selected exactly through \(|h|=h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\).  Bloemendal and Virag (2013) study near-edge laws, whereas the critical point here remains a unique first-order selection.  Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026) motivate weak-factor-robust inference but exclude the rank-one block treatment through non-collinearity.  Cardoso, Ferman, and Fernandes (2026) establish the strong treatment-factor bad-control endpoint, not the bounded local phase or its exact reach condition.  Bai and Ng (2021) motivate observed-block imputation, and Gobillon and Magnac (2016) motivate comparing whole-sample and counterfactual factor fits; the present exact-oracle result is a sensitivity benchmark rather than a direct empirical identification claim.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The four exact orthogonality restrictions define the admissible triangular-array class.  They eliminate baseline-factor cross terms and isolate absorption by the fitted singular direction, but they are not observable residualization conditions.  Within this class the scalar profile has an always-separated singleton, including at \(|h|=h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\).  An absorbed region exists in the bounded experiment only when \(\overline h>\min_{\eta}h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\); no signal-reach assumption is imposed to force that inequality.
body.honest_scope: The proposal is an abstract exact-oracle sensitivity benchmark.  All stochastic profile, selection, absorption, and Wald conclusions concern \(\theta\in[-K,K]\) and \(h=\theta/\sigma\in[-\overline h,\overline h]\).  There is no genuine tie in this domain: the coefficient equals the ATT coordinate at and below the explicit threshold and lies strictly between the ATT coordinate and zero above it.  The absorbed phase may be empty, and it is nonempty exactly when \(\overline h>\min_{\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}}h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\).  Exact finite-array orthogonality is a defining restriction, not an observable procedure.  Masked fitting is only an internal control, not a claimed new practical estimator, and no stochastic conclusion is extended to unbounded \(|h|\).
